summary:
Sonora is a state of Mexico and stands under the national framework of Mexico, which carries the country-level legal and enforcement picture; the findings below are those of the state itself.

Sonora's Congress approved the Ley de Identidad de Género on 1 October 2020, the Hermosillo daily El Sol de Hermosillo reported at the time, creating a state procedure for people who identify with the opposite gender to modify their official documentation. Wikipedia's LGBT rights in Mexico page lists Sonora among 25 Mexican states with a gender identity law dated to 2020 and describes the statute as giving trans people a statutory route to rectify gender on civil documents.

The state's protections extend past documents. On 6 December 2022 Sonora's Congress banned conversion therapies (ECOSIG). Sonora's hate-crime legislation recognises motivation by gender and sexual preference as an aggravating factor, and the state ratified the 2011 constitutional amendment prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation.

Marriage between partners of the same legal sex is available in Sonora; by 31 December 2022 every Mexican state, Sonora included, had legalised it by legislation, executive order or judicial ruling. A trans visitor whose relationship would be locally classed as same-sex falls under the same recognition.

No source in the inventory records how these provisions are enforced in Sonora, and no trans-specific violence or incident data for the state was identified. The formal protections exist on the statute book; the state-level enforcement record is undocumented in these sources.
tangentialFactors:
The 2020 statute is described as allowing people who identify with the opposite gender to modify official documentation, a formulation that frames eligibility in binary and documentary terms rather than as self-declared identity.

The state statute governs residents' civil documents. A visitor's identity documents are governed by their home jurisdiction, so the Sonora procedure has no bearing on a visitor's paperwork even where the state's broader protections apply.
localsOnly:
Residents of Sonora can apply under the Ley de Identidad de Género approved on 1 October 2020 to change gender on official documentation; the procedure is a state civil-documents route and is not available to visitors, who must use the processes of their own jurisdiction.

Residents also have the December 2022 prohibition on conversion therapies (ECOSIG), hate-crime provisions covering gender and sexual-preference motivation, and the 2011 constitutional anti-discrimination amendment ratified by the state. Marriage between partners of the same legal sex has been available in Sonora since at least 31 December 2022, when every Mexican state had legalised it.
outOfScopeNotes:
The tally of states with gender-recognition procedures is unresolved: the counts published by Human Rights Watch and by Wikipedia differ, and neither resolves whether Sonora's 2020 law is included in the lower figure.

How the state procedure operates in practice is not sourced: its processing times, documentary requirements, whether it is administrative or judicial, and any record of refusals or delays in Sonora do not appear in the inventory.
